title: Mobile crane
prompt: A labelled scale teaching model of the page 57 mobile crane has a wheeled chassis, outrigger beams and jacks, telescopic boom, visible boom-raising hydraulic ram, base counterweight and cable block and tackle. Stabilize extends the beams and lowers the jacks onto the support surface. Extend shows the telescopic sections moving to a chosen supported reach as an externally actuated teaching motion, without claiming unsourced extension internals. Hoist uses the reeved cable and load block to raise a small weight within that setup. See-through exposes the pictured load-bearing parts and rope route. Do not add a complete hydraulic circuit or invent extension cylinders hidden inside the boom.
blurb: A scale teaching adaptation of a mobile crane shows its outriggers, boom-raising ram, telescopic sections and reeved lifting rope.
truthNotes: Tabletop scale teaching model, not an exact book reconstruction.
Telescopic extension is externally actuated teaching motion. No internal extension actuator, pump or valve circuit is claimed.
Two supporting rope strands simplify the pictured tackle; the base drum takes up twice the load travel.
The model requires stabilization before boom extension and lifting. Extension pays out rope to keep the weight clear.
The small weight is a teaching specimen and the board a fixture; neither is counted as anatomy.
The accepted 1998 text and 2016 page support the mechanism. The 1988 edition remains inaccessible and unverified. No edition-union claim.

verification.telemetry: n/a. Standalone static figure has no production telemetry.
